episodes.rule: Never answer when the woods call your name.
episodes.title: Never Answer the Woods | Hollowmere Tales EP 1
episodes.summary: Odo and Mothwick carry the last flame through Hollowmere while something calls with his lost sister Wren's voice; they escape the Gloamhounds and riddle past the Wick-eaters. episodes.theme: True story: the Flannan Isles lighthouse keepers (Scotland, 1900)
episodes.rule: The records say what was found; the legends add what wasn't.
episodes.title: The Lighthouse Keepers Who Vanished | True Story | Hollowmere Tales EP 2
episodes.summary: In December 1900 the new lighthouse on Eilean Mor went dark; when the Hesperus arrived on 26 December, keepers Ducat, Marshall and McArthur were gone, lamps ready, clock stopped, one set of oilskins left behind. Superintendent Muirhead concluded a huge sea swept them away; no one was ever found, and the later 'meal on the table' details came from a 1912 poem.
episodes.cliffhanger: Moth: some true stories never end — the island kept their secret.

episodes.theme: True story: the Lost Colony of Roanoke (North Carolina, 1587-1590)
episodes.rule: If you must leave, carve where you went — and a cross if you're in danger.
episodes.title: The Colony That Vanished | True Story | Hollowmere Tales EP 3
episodes.summary: About 115 settlers landed on Roanoke Island in 1587; governor John White sailed home for supplies and war with Spain kept him away three years. On 18 August 1590, Virginia Dare's third birthday, he found the colony gone, 'CRO' on a tree and 'CROATOAN' on a palisade post with no cross, and a storm stopped him searching.
episodes.cliffhanger: Over a hundred people and a three-year-old girl, never seen again.

episodes.theme: True story: the Mary Celeste (Atlantic Ocean, 1872)
episodes.rule: Never leave a ship that can still float.
episodes.title: The Ship Found With No One Aboard | True Story | Hollowmere Tales EP 4
episodes.summary: The Mary Celeste left New York on 7 November 1872 with Captain Benjamin Briggs, his wife Sarah, daughter Sophia (2) and seven crew; the last log entry (25 Nov) had Santa Maria in the Azores in sight. On 5 December the Dei Gratia found her drifting and seaworthy, food and belongings aboard, ~3.5 ft of water in the hold, one pump dismantled and the only lifeboat gone; no one was ever found.
episodes.cliffhanger: Moth: somewhere out there, the sea is still keeping its secret.

episodes.theme: True story: the Devil's Footprints (Devon, England, February 1855)
episodes.title: What Walked Over the Rooftops in 1855?
episodes.summary: After snow on the night of 8-9 February 1855, towns around the Exe estuary (Topsham, Lympstone, Exmouth, Dawlish, Teignmouth) found single-file hoof-shaped prints about 4 x 3 inches that went over walls and roofs, stopped at a haystack and resumed beyond it. Theories ranged from badgers (Richard Owen) to Rev. Musgrave's kangaroo, which he later admitted he suggested to calm people; nothing was ever explained.
episodes.cliffhanger: On 13 February new prints appeared in Topsham churchyard - and they lead right to Odo and Mothwick.

episodes.theme: Recorded legend: the Bell Witch (Robertson County, Tennessee, 1817-1821; written in full by M. V. Ingram, 1894)
episodes.title: Who Was Talking Inside the Walls?
episodes.summary: From 1817 the Bell family farm near the Red River heard knocking, scratching and gnawing, then a voice that sang, quoted scripture and called everyone by name; they called it Kate. It warned Betsy not to marry Joshua Gardner, left in 1821 promising to return in seven years and, the story says, came back in 1828; the Andrew Jackson visit is unproven and sceptics suspect a hoax.
episodes.cliffhanger: The knocking starts behind the wall again - and the voice says: 'Odo... I know your name.'

episodes.theme: Recorded legend + real newspaper panic: the Jersey Devil (Leeds Point legend of 1735; sightings week 16-23 January 1909, South Jersey / Philadelphia)
episodes.title: What Was Screaming in the Pine Barrens?
episodes.summary: Legend says Mother Leeds' 13th child (Leeds Point, 1735) grew wings and hooves and flew up the chimney into the Pine Barrens. In the week of 16-23 January 1909 newspapers printed hundreds of reports - tracks over fences and rooftops, a winged horse-headed thing, police in Camden and Bristol PA firing at it - schools closed and posses searched; some tracks were hoaxes and historians call it mass panic, but nothing was ever caught.
episodes.cliffhanger: Fresh hoof prints in the swamp mud stop right behind Odo and Mothwick - card 'WHAT LIVES IN THE PINES?'

episodes.theme: Recorded legend: Black Shuck, the black dog of Bungay and Blythburgh (Suffolk, Sunday 4 August 1577; Abraham Fleming's pamphlet 'A Straunge and Terrible Wunder', 1577)
episodes.title: What Burst Through the Church Door in 1577?
episodes.summary: On 4 August 1577 a violent storm hit Bungay; Fleming's pamphlet says a black dog appeared in St Mary's Church with flashes of fire and ran through the congregation, and the same day it burst into Holy Trinity, Blythburgh, where the spire fell through the roof. Scorch marks on Blythburgh's north door ('the Devil's fingerprints') are still shown; historians point to a lightning storm, sceptics to candle burns.
episodes.cliffhanger: On the coast road, giant paw prints circle Odo and Mothwick - card 'WHAT WALKS THE COAST ROAD?'

episodes.theme: True record + legend: the children of Hamelin (Lower Saxony, Germany, 26 June 1284; church window c.1300 destroyed 1660; Lueneburg manuscript c.1440-50; rats added c.1559; Bungelosenstrasse)
episodes.title: Where Did Hamelin's 130 Children Go?
episodes.summary: On 26 June 1284, records say a piper 'clothed in many kinds of colours' led 130 children of Hamelin away near the Koppen hill, and they were never seen again; a church window of c.1300 showed it, the rats were only added around 1559. Music is still banned on Bungelosenstrasse; historians suggest emigration east, a pilgrimage or dancing mania, but no one knows.
episodes.cliffhanger: Small footprints lead up the hill and none come back; the piper lunges out of the dark - card 'WHO WAS THE PIPER?'

episodes.theme: True story: the dancing plague of 1518 (Strasbourg, Alsace; Frau Troffea from 14 July 1518; guild halls and stages in the horse and grain markets with paid musicians; drum/dance ban; red shoes at the shrine of St Vitus, Saverne; ended by early September)
episodes.title: Why Couldn't Strasbourg Stop Dancing?
episodes.summary: On 14 July 1518 Frau Troffea began to dance in a Strasbourg street with no music and could not stop; within days 30+ joined and by August chroniclers counted 50-400 dancers. The council's cure (guild halls, stages, paid musicians) only spread it; then music was banned and dancers were sent to St Vitus at Saverne for red shoes and crosses - ergot vs. mass psychogenic illness, no one knows.
episodes.cliffhanger: Drums from the empty square; a dancer lunges out of the dark - card 'WHO STARTS THE DANCE?'

episodes.theme: True story: the Carroll A. Deering ghost ship (five-masted schooner, Bath, Maine 1919; hailed the Cape Lookout lightship late Jan 1921 - red-haired man, lost anchors; found aground on Diamond Shoals off Cape Hatteras at dawn 31 Jan 1921, all sails set; boarded 4 Feb: crew, lifeboats, log, navigation gear gone, food in the galley; fake bottle note April 1921; dynamited March 1921; bell at the Graveyard of the Atlantic Museum)
episodes.rule: If a ship waves at you tonight, don't wave back.
episodes.title: Why Was This Ship Found With No Crew?
episodes.summary: Coming home from Brazil in January 1921, the schooner Carroll A. Deering passed the Cape Lookout lightship, where a red-haired man shouted that she had lost her anchors. Two days later she was found on Diamond Shoals with every sail set and no one aboard; the crew, lifeboats and log were never found.
episodes.cliffhanger: The Deering's bell sits in a museum - yet Odo hears it ringing on the water, and the red-haired man shouts again.
